1.d: father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application
1.k: chief, (fore-) father(-less), [idiom] patrimony, principal. Compare names in 'Abi-'.

6.d: properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy)
6.k: break, destroy(-uction), [phrase] not escape, fail, lose, (cause to, make) perish, spend, [idiom] and surely, take, be undone, [idiom] utterly, be void of, have no way to flee.

7.d: {properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy)}

9.d: concrete, something lost; abstract, destruction, i.e. Hades

10.o: the same as H9 (אֲבֵדָה), miswritten for H11 (אֲבַדּוֹן);

14.d: to breathe after, i.e. (figuratively) to be acquiescent
14.k: consent, rest content will, be willing.

16.o: from H14 (אָבָה) (in the sense of bending toward);

17.o: from H14 (אָבָה) (in the sense of desiring);

19.o: from an unused root (apparently meaning to turn);

22.d: Abiel, the name of two Israelites
22.o: from H1 (אָב) and H410 (אֵל); father (i.e. possessor) of God;

23.o: from H1 (אָב) and H622 (אָסַף); father of gathering (i.e. gatherer);

24.d: green, i.e. a young ear of grain; hence, the name of the month Abib or Nisan
24.k: Abib, ear, green ears of corn (not maize).
24.o: from an unused root (meaning to be tender);

25.o: from H1 (אָב) and H1391 (גִּבְעוֹן); father (i.e. founder) of Gibon;

26.d: Abigail or Abigal, the name of two Israelitesses
26.o: or shorter אֲבִיגַל; from H1 (אָב) and H1524 (גִּיל); father (i.e. source) of joy;

27.o: from H1 (אָב) and H1777 (דִּין); father of judgment (i.e. judge);

28.d: Abida, a son of Abraham by Keturah
28.o: from H1 (אָב) and H3045 (יָדַע); father of knowledge (i.e. knowing);

29.d: Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses
29.o: or prolonged אֲבִיָּהוּ ; from H1 (אָב) and H3050 (יָהּ); father (i.e. worshipper) of Jah;

30.o: from H1 (אָב) and H1931 (הוּא); father (i.e. worshipper) of Him (i.e. God);

31.d: Abihud, the name of two Israelites
31.o: from H1 (אָב) and H1935 (הוֹד); father (i.e. possessor) of renown;

32.d: Abihail or Abichail, the name of three Israelites and two Israelitesses
32.o: or (more correctly) אֲבִיחַיִל ; from H1 (אָב) and H2428 (חַיִל); father (i.e. possessor) of might;

33.d: an Abiezrite or descendant of Abiezer
33.o: from H44 (אֲבִיעֶזֶר) with the article inserted; father of the Ezrite;

34.o: from H14 (אָבָה), in the sense of want (especially in feeling);

35.d: provocative of desire; the caper berry (from its stimulative taste)

36.o: from H1 (אָב) and H2898 (טוּב); father of goodness (i.e. good);

37.d: Abital, a wife of King David
37.o: from H1 (אָב) and H2919 (טַל); father of dew (i.e. fresh);

38.d: Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah
38.o: from H1 (אָב) and H3220 (יָם); father of (the) sea (i.e. seaman);

39.o: from H1 (אָב) and an elsewhere unused (probably foreign) word; father of Mael (apparently some Arab tribe);

40.d: Abimelek, the name of two Philistine kings and of two Israelites
40.o: from H1 (אָב) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); father of (the) king;

41.d: Abinadab, the name of four Israelites
41.o: from H1 (אָב) and H5068 (נָדַב); father of generosity (i.e. liberal);

42.o: from H1 (אָב) and H5278 (נֹעַם); father of pleasantness (i.e. gracious);

44.d: Abiezer, the name of two Israelites
44.o: from H1 (אָב) and H5829 (עֵזֶר); father of help (i.e. helpful);

45.o: from H1 (אָב) and an unused root of uncertain derivation; probably, father of strength (i.e. valiant);

47.k: angel, bull, chiefest, mighty (one), stout(-hearted), strong (one), valiant.

48.d: Abiram, the name of two Israelites
48.o: from H1 (אָב) and H7311 (רוּם); father of height (i.e. lofty);

49.o: from H1 (אָב) and H7686 (שָׁגָה); father of error (i.e. blundering);

50.d: Abishua, the name of two Israelites
50.o: from H1 (אָב) and H7771 (שׁוֹעַ); father of plenty (i.e. prosperous);

51.o: from H1 (אָב) and H7791 (שׁוּר); father of (the) wall (i.e. perhaps mason);

52.o: or (shorter) אַבְשַׁי ; from H1 (אָב) and H7862 (שַׁי); father of a gift (i.e. probably generous);

53.d: Abshalom, a son of David; also (the fuller form) a later Israelite
53.o: or (shortened) אַבְשָׁלוֹם ; from H1 (אָב) and H7965 (שָׁלוֹם); father of peace (i.e. friendly);

54.o: contracted from H1 (אָב) and H3498 (יָתַר); father of abundance (i.e. liberal);

58.k: plain. Compare also the proper names beginning with Abel-.
58.o: from an unused root (meaning to be grassy);

59.d: Abel, the name of two places in Palestine.

61.o: apparently from H56 (אָבַל) through the idea of negation;

62.d: Abel of Beth-maakah, a place in Palestine
62.o: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H1004 (בַּיִת) and H4601 (מַעֲכָה); meadow of Beth-Maakah;

63.d: Abel hash-Shittim, a place in Palestine
63.o: from H58 (אָבֵל) and the plural of H7848 (שִׁטָּה), with the article inserted; meadow of the acacias;

64.o: from H58 (אָבֵל) and the plural of H3754 (כֶּרֶם); meadow of vineyards;

65.o: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H4246 (מְחֹלָה)xlit mᵉchôwlâh corrected to mᵉchôlâh; meadow of dancing;

66.o: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H4325 (מַיִם); meadow of water;

67.o: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H4714 (מִצְרַיִם); meadow of Egypt;

68.k: [phrase] carbuncle, [phrase] mason, [phrase] plummet, (chalk-, hail-, head-, sling-) stone(-ny), (divers) weight(-s).
68.o: from the root of H1129 (בָּנָה) through the meaning to build;

70.d: a pair of stones (only dual); a potter's wheel or a midwife's stool (consisting alike of two horizontal disks with a support between)

71.o: perhaps feminine of H68 (אֶבֶן); stony;  Compare H549 (אֲמָנָה).

72.o: from H68 (אֶבֶן) and H5828 (עֵזֶר) with the article inserted; stone of the help;

74.o: or (fully) אֲבִינֵר ; from H1 (אָב) and H5216 (נִיר); father of light (i.e. enlightening);

76.o: (by reduplication) from an unused root (meaning to belch forth);

77.o: from an unused root probably meaning to gleam; conspicuous;

78.o: from the same as H76 (אֲבַעְבֻּעָה); splendid;

79.o: a primitive root, probably to float away (as vapor), but used only as denominative from H80 (אָבָק);

85.d: Abraham, the later name of Abram
85.o: contracted from H1 (אָב) and an unused root (probably meaning to be populous); father of a multitude;

87.d: Abram, the original name of Abraham

88.d: Oboth, a place in the Desert

90.d: Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings
90.o: or אֲגָג; of uncertain derivation (compare H89 (אָגֵא)); flame;

91.d: an Agagite or descendent (subject) of Agag

92.d: a band, bundle, knot, or arch
92.o: feminine passive participle of an unused root (meaning to bind);

94.d: Agur, a fanciful name for Solomon
94.o: passive participle of H103 (אָגַר); gathered (i.e. received among the sages);

95.d: properly, something gathered, i.e. perhaps a grain or berry; used only of a small (silver) coin

96.o: from an unused root (meaning to flow down or together as drops);

97.o: dual of H96 (אֶגֶל).; a double pond;

98.d: a marsh; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds
98.o: from an unused root (meaning to collect as water);

99.o: probably from the same as H98 (אֲגַם) (in the sense of stagnant water);
